Consistency before complexity, every time.

Something clicks differently when a child hears a new word inside a song, a game, or a rhyme — versus just being told what it means.
The context does the teaching. The fun is just the delivery system.
That's why early English exposure works best when kids don't realize it's a lesson at all.

body:
ESL grammar is tricky to sequence — not because the rules are hard, but because the order you introduce them matters more than most people realize.
A wrong sequencing choice early on and kids hit a wall they don't have the vocabulary to explain.
That pacing problem is the whole backbone of Little Learners' English Grammar.

body:
When a child says "I don't want to do this anymore," they're not always rejecting the activity.
Sometimes they're telling you they need to feel less watched.
Backing off a little — not giving up on them, just giving them room — changes everything.
No-pressure learning isn't lowering the bar. It's widening the door. 🚪

The tricky part of designing a low-pressure activity isn't making it easy — it's making it feel like there's no wrong move.
When a child senses they can't fail, they actually try harder. That's the tension the whole structure is built around.
That thinking is behind Little Words, Big Discoveries.

A child who keeps making the same 'mistake' in a sentence isn't stuck — they're running an experiment.
They need to hear it land wrong a few times before the right version feels true.
That's not failure. That's how the pattern actually gets built.
